walkthroughs.body_html: HACCP is a structured system used in UK food businesses. It identifies food safety hazards — biological, chemical, physical — and sets Critical Control Points (CCPs) where each hazard must be removed or reduced to safe levels.

HACCP has seven principles: conduct hazard analysis, identify CCPs, set critical limits, monitor CCPs, set corrective actions, verify the system works, and keep records. Together they create a paper trail of safe practice.

Examples of monitoring: a probe thermometer checks chicken hits 75 °C in its centre; fridge temperatures are logged twice daily; deliveries are checked against use-by dates. Every log is part of the HACCP record.
